title: Positive object cohomology of tensor-sections sheaves vanishes on affine opens
statement: For a scheme X with small-coefficient sheafification and Ext as in the Lean signature, a quasi-coherent module F on X, a natural number n and every affine open U of X, the (n+1)-st etale object cohomology of the associated tensor-sections sheaf at the etale object U is zero. No vanishing on non-affine opens is asserted.

source.place: Tag 03P2 (affine case); sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 03F3; official source https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03P2

proof.text: Fix an affine open U, choose an injective resolution R of F_et, and apply lem-sc-etale-ulift-injective-resolution to obtain a resolution S of its coefficient lift together with the evaluation-complex comparison at U.

Put A = upperStar along U.ι with large coefficients. The extension-by-zero adjunction and its exactness imply that A preserves injectives. Apply A degreewise to S, with the transported augmentation, to construct an injective resolution S′ of A(F_et lifted).

Inverse-image localization restriction commutes definitionally with coefficient lift. Lift the open quasi-coherent identification to identify A(F_et lifted) with the lift of the tensor-sections sheaf of F restricted to U. Mathlib isQuasicoherent_restrictFunctor gives quasi-coherence of the restricted module; hU is exactly IsAffine U.toScheme. Apply lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent in degree n+1 to this lifted sheaf. Functoriality of Sheaf.H transports zero to H(A(F_et lifted),n+1).

The terminal object T of the open etale site is the identity of U. Apply new-sheaf-cohomology-derived-evaluation and S′.isoRightDerivedObj to conclude that the evaluation complex of S′ at T has zero homology. The localization functor sends T to the open etale object because id_U composed with U.ι is U.ι. Whisker the inverse-image/restriction isomorphism with terminal evaluation and use naturality of a sheaf map along this object equality to obtain A followed by terminal evaluation isomorphic to evaluation at U. Map this functor isomorphism on complexes and homology to conclude that S evaluated at U has zero homology.

Take homology of the coefficient-lift evaluation comparison from step 1. The Mathlib mapHomologicalComplexCompIso and ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso identify it with ULift of the homology of R evaluated at U. ULift.up is injective, hence zero of the lifted additive group implies the original evaluated homology is subsingleton. Apply lem-weil-pbc-object-cohomology-presheaf-resolution to R, evaluate its lifted presheaf isomorphism at U, and use preservation of homology by presheaf evaluation to identify its right side with that zero group. Reflect subsingleton once more by ULift.up and use AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton. This includes the empty open and n=0; no non-affine vanishing is asserted.

mathlib_searches.results: AffineZariskiSite.sheafEquiv and standard affine section localization lemmas; no object-cohomology affine acyclicity theorem

Mathlib supplies cohomologyPresheaf and local-injectivity/sheafification tools. Repository supplies etale_affine_qcoherent_succ and objectCohomologyPresheaf_resolution. PushedResolutionPositiveHomologyZero is a related proved argument, but its Scheme.{u+1} interface does not instantiate at arbitrary Scheme.{u}; this criterion uses its generic resolution dependency and the same universe-transport argument. No duplicate of affine-open tensor object acyclicity found.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleTensorPositiveObjectCohomology
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasSheafify X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → IsZero
      (Sheaf.H' (etaleTensorSectionsSheaf F) (n + 1)
        (Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι))
